record.original_question: For each dimension d, what is the greatest possible volume of a pair of spherical space forms, that is, manifold quotients of the round sphere, that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 1.6. What is the largest volume of an isospectral and non-isometric pair of d-dimensional spherical space forms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ denote the round unit $d$-sphere with its standard Riemannian metric. A spherical space form of dimension $d$ is a Riemannian manifold of the form $\Gamma \backslash S^d$, where $\Gamma$ is a finite subgroup of the orthogonal group $O(d+1)$ acting freely on $S^d$. Two Riemannian manifolds are Laplace-isospectral if their Laplace–Beltrami operators acting on smooth functions have the same eigenvalue spectrum (with multiplicities), and they are isometric if there exists a Riemannian isometry between them.

For each integer $d \ge 2$, determine the supremum
$$V(d) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{\, \operatorname{vol}(M) \;:\; \text{there exists a spherical space form } M' \text{ of dimension } d \text{ with } M \text{ and } M' \text{ Laplace-isospectral but not isometric} \,\bigr\}, $$
and decide whether this supremum is attained.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024/2025 preprint, "Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume," directly addresses this question. It establishes a lower bound of $\operatorname{vol}(S^d)/8$ for the largest volume of an isospectral non-isometric pair (in the orbifold setting via almost conjugate subgroups isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^3$), and shows non-existence in low dimensions ($d \le 4$) for lens orbifolds, but the exact value of the largest volume for spherical space forms in general dimension remains open.

status_evidence.title: Isospectral spherical space forms and orbifolds of highest volume
status_evidence.snippet: The spherical analog of the question of finding isospectral hyperbolic orbifolds of smallest volume is finding isospectral spherical orbifolds of largest volume. A pair of almost conjugate subgroups yields isospectral non-isometric pairs with vol(S^d)/8 as a lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of the largest volume of an isospectral non-isometric pair of d-dimensional spherical space forms is studied; partial bounds and low-dimensional non-existence results exist, but the exact answer is not known in general.

status_evidence.title: On spherical space forms which are isospectral but not isometric
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of isospectral non-isometric spherical space forms via almost conjugate subgroups.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of isospectral non-isometric spherical space forms have been constructed, but they do not determine the maximal volume.
